overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance for FACTVERSE reveals a clear dominance of extreme space and planetary 'What If' scenarios over standard psychological or animal facts. Videos featuring hypothetical planetary falls, exotic planetary conditions (such as diamond, dark, or burning ice worlds), and counterintuitive cosmic phenomena generate significantly higher views-per-day and like ratios (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y, 8KEl0_pJ_68, 6pwazIPnOHw) compared to static psychological tricks or common animal trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) lead in velocity with over 1000 views and strong engagement within days of release.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, immersive space 'What If' scenarios combining extreme physical environments with second-person framing.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme planetary conditions ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') capture robust view counts and high likes-per-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize lesser-known, visually dramatic astronomical phenomena that challenge everyday logic over basic biological facts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal human psychology or memory tricks (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') consistently underperform in views-per-day and engagement metrics.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia or reduce their frequency, shifting production focus towards high-visual-potential space and physical science.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into a Star Made Entirely of Neon?
next_video.opening_direction: Start directly with the violent, blinding descent into a neon-core star, using vivid, high-contrast visual cues to immediately lock viewer attention.

next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of 'What If You Fell Into...' space formats while exploring a completely fresh chemical and stellar phenomenon not yet covered.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond, dark, burning ice, or liquid metal planets
Must use a newly introduced celestial body or element

experiment: Test a 15-second pacing structure on a brand-new space anomaly topic, removing all introductory fluff and starting mid-action on the hypothetical drop to measure retention impact against standard 21-second formats.
